'''Paul L. McPherson''' (born July 3, 1978) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player.

A {{convert|6|ft|4|in|m|adj=on}} [[shooting guard]] from [[Chicago]]'s [[South Shore High School (Chicago)|South Shore High School]], McPherson played at [[Tallahassee Community College]], [[Kennedy-King College]], and [[DePaul University]] before being signed by the [[Phoenix Suns]] of the [[National Basketball Association]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/suns/news/mcpherson_000823.html Suns sign Paul McPherson]. at NBA.com</ref> McPherson played a total of 55 games in his NBA career, all during the [[2000–01 NBA season]], playing 33 games with the Suns and 22 with the [[Golden State Warriors]]. His career averages are 4.8 [[points per game]] and 1.4 [[rebounds per game]]. His final NBA game was played on April 18, 2001, in an 81 - 95 loss to the Vancouver Grizzlies where he played 10 and half minutes and the only stat he recorded was 1 rebound.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mcphepa01.html Paul McPherson]. basketball-reference.com</ref>

After his brief stint in the NBA, McPherson played in the American [[minor league]]s and overseas.<ref>[http://www.eurobasket.com/player.asp?Cntry=ita&PlayerID=29101 Paul McPherson] at EuroBasket.com</ref> He also spent part of the 2002-2003 basketball season touring with the [[Harlem Globetrotters]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/wolves/summer_2005_paul_mcpherson.html Paul McPherson bio] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090301173454/http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/wolves/summer_2005_paul_mcpherson.html |date=2009-03-01 }} at NBA.com</ref>

Furthermore. he reached the Semifinal of the Nike King of the World Battleground 2004 and won $10000, but could not get to the final.

Paul McPherson,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Englewood basketball coach Paul McPherson, a former NBA player, jailed on multiple charges |url=https://www.jacksonville.com/story/news/crime/2023/10/26/jacksonville-basketball-coach-and-formepaul-mcpherson-a-former-nba-player-jailed-on-multiple-charges/71333945007/ |access-date=2023-11-20 |website=The Florida Times-Union |language=en-US}}</ref> was charged with four counts of unlawful sexual activity with a minor, three counts of contributing to the delinquency of a minor and one count each of possession of less than 20 grams of marijuana and unlawful use of a two-way communications device, according to his jail and arrest report. While McPherson was serving as the Englewood High School Boys Basketball coach and as the school's security guard.
